question: Can an action-independent prequential calibration residual diagnose misspecified causal families more accurately than Gate14's individual surprise-bit guard, preserving true-pair learning under matched intervention budget and controls?
mathematical_correction: For Gate13's 113-hypothesis family, all deterministic hypotheses assign conditional observation probabilities .05/.95, so conditional entropy h(.05) is constant; the fair-coin null has h(.5) but its posterior mass is independent of candidate action. Consequently expected conditional entropy is action-invariant and expected hypothesis-label mutual information differs from predictive entropy only by a state-dependent additive constant: the action argmax rankings are identical. Do not treat 'MI' as a new distinct action arm here.

data.source_family: Gate13 exact 113-hypothesis Bayesian source, source 2-parent or unary; OOD 3-parent parity or independent fair-label; 5% sensor flip on nonrandom
data.common_noise: deterministic source output keyed by seed/context/action/visit, same if actions match
data.held: all 32 action vectors, disjoint noise domain, outcomes never used for training, active selection, or controls

models.posterior: All policies use exactly the Gate13 113-hypothesis posterior (3 null p=.05,.5,.95; 10 unary; 100 pair) and predeclared equal third-mass priors; same log posterior likelihood updates and 113 logits per world.
models.residual_guard: At each observed training event compute p in pre-update model for selected action. Excess Brier s=(p-y)^2 - p(1-p); accumulate s over context. After at least 6 observations, if mean accumulated excess >0.06, set sticky adequacy alarm. When alarmed choose balanced schedule rather than active entropy search, and for held forecast mix 45% fair null: p=0.55*p_model+0.225. Otherwise use active actions and unshrunk model predictions. No probe actions reserved.
models.active: Gate13 original entropy-max intervention (tie fewest visits, then smallest x); unshrunk posterior prediction.
models.random: Gate13 seed/context/step independent uniform action selection, allowing repeats.
models.fixed_damp: Exactly Gate13 active interventions with non-adaptive 30% fair-null held shrinkage p=0.7*p_model+0.15; determines whether conditional alarms beat a trivial fixed defensive forecast.

capacity: Each policy retains for two contexts: 113 float64 log scores +32 uint8 visit counters +1 uint8 step +1 float64 accumulated excess +1 uint8 alarm, totaling 946 bytes per context, 1892 bytes total; all policies allocate same full record, even when not using alarm. Temporary candidate arrays and model code not counted.
evidence: All five policies compute all 32 candidate posterior forecasts each training step (equalized counted hypothesis work, artificial overhead for balanced/random); controls share actions/outcome function/budget, not necessarily identical selected observations; per-family 64 or 32 new seed trials. Model outcomes sealed source before run.
cold: After training A then B, require dormant A state unchanged, pack all policies to exact 1892 bytes, restore independently twice and resume four interventions of A; every selected action, observed y, model posterior serialization and predictions must match bitwise. This is synthetic same-process cold continuation, not native cold storage.
measurements: held per-world Brier mean for all five arms, paired seed normal 95% CI
false alarms in genuine pair/unary contexts and OOD alarm rate
guard Brier gain vs active, balanced/random and fixed damping
all same-budget action count and candidate-hypothesis evaluation counts
exact checkpoint bytes and continued-action equality
qualification: Development-only supported if every prespecified threshold passes. Any failure is MIXED/NO-GO, not SCIENTIFIC_PASS. Fully qualified Yggdrasil native model gain requires a separate owner-controlled experiment with strong conventional comparators and native checkpoint custody.
